findings.description: storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volume, snapshots and logs, so all catalog data is stored in cleartext.

publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance an internet-routable endpoint, moving the database outside the private subnet boundary and leaving the security group as the only control; the endpoint is also published as a Terraform output.

Neither the instance nor aws_db_parameter_group.catalog_db_params sets require_secure_transport, and the generated PHP client uses plain mysqli_connect, so credentials and query data can traverse the network unencrypted - particularly serious given the public endpoint.

The RDS master password (var.password) is interpolated into user_data, which is readable in cleartext from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF in the hosted PHP app, and is stored unencrypted in Terraform state.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled; a server-side request forgery in the PHP application would yield the highly privileged instance-profile credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the EBS volume holding /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc (which contains the database password in cleartext) is unencrypted at rest.

Inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached to the internet-facing web server, allowing full account-wide data access and privilege escalation (e.g. modifying security groups, launching instances, reading all buckets) if the host is compromised.
The database security group permits all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0 outbound, providing an unconstrained exfiltration and command-and-control path from the database tier.

skip_final_snapshot = true combined with backup_retention_period = 0 disables point-in-time recovery and any final snapshot, meaning data destruction (accidental or via the wildcard rds:* permissions granted to the app role) is unrecoverable.
